about: The end-to-end scenarios for a DataPipe deployment, as data rather than prose. site/index.html renders its "What to check" list from this file, and the e2e-testbed skill in the datapipe repo drives it. Add `experiment`, `base` and `run` to each scenario's params to build a URL.
observed: Parts of this manifest were checked against https://datapipe-test.web.app at commit a10464c on 2026-09-19. Each scenario carries an `observed` field saying what that run actually saw. Everything else is derived from the handler code and is still unconfirmed against a live deployment.

defaults.resultContract: Read `document.documentElement.dataset.testbedStatus` and the JSON text of `#testbed-result` from the DOM. `window.__testbed` holds the same object, but a browser extension evaluating JavaScript in an isolated world may not see a page global -- prefer the DOM.

preconditions.experiment: A fresh experiment on the deployment under test, storing to Google Drive (new experiments cannot choose OSF). Record its ID.
preconditions.dataCollection: "Accept new data" ON, except where a scenario says otherwise.
preconditions.validation: LEAVE THE DEFAULTS ALONE -- no setup needed. A new experiment ships with validation ON and one required field, `trial_type` (create-experiment.ts: `useValidation ?? true`, `requiredFields ?? ["trial_type"]`). Both pages satisfy it: jsPsych writes `trial_type` itself from each plugin's `info.name`, and the plain-JavaScript page puts `trial_type: "letter-keyboard-response"` on every row. If a scenario is unexpectedly refused with 400 INVALID_DATA, this is where to look. `validation-failure` is the one scenario that omits the column on purpose.
preconditions.metadata: "Generate Psych-DS metadata" LOCKS PERMANENTLY once the experiment has data ("Locked because this experiment has collected data"). Decide before the first submission. With it on, raw files move from the folder root to data/raw/, derived CSVs appear beside them, and a submission that is not parseable CSV/JSON is refused with METADATA_ERROR.
preconditions.conditions: "Assign conditions in sequence" OFF by default; the condition scenarios switch it.
preconditions.base64: "Accept base64 file uploads" OFF by default; the base64 scenarios switch it.

ordering.rule: Run scenarios in `order`. A scenario that changes experiment-level state (`mutatesExperimentState`) affects every scenario after it, and one with `mustRunLast` must not run before the scenarios in its `runAfter` have met their `runAfterCondition`.
ordering.why: Observed 2026-09-19: switching "Accept new data" off for `closed-experiment` while an earlier session was still staged DESTROYED that session's recovery. The staging sweep re-checks the experiment before promoting anything (scheduled-staging-sweep.ts, "THE SECOND DOOR") and discards staged trials outright when `active` is false. The run then looked like a recovery bug that does not exist.
ordering.alternative: Run `closed-experiment` on a second throwaway experiment instead, and the ordering constraint goes away.

timingFacts.sweepCron: */5 (staging sweep and upload retry every tick; pending recovery on the :00/:15/:30/:45 slots; mail retry on :00/:10/...)
timingFacts.note: A recovered session is QUEUED by the sweep, not uploaded by it. queue-upload.ts gives an entry with no provider error code nextRetryAt = now + 1 hour, and the retry worker runs on */5 -- so a partial file reaches storage roughly 65-75 minutes after the participant dropped out, not 15. For that hour the dashboard's queue panel describes it as an upload that did not go through, with retryCount 0 and lastAttemptAt null. That is expected, not a bug.
timingFacts.whenTheClockStarts: For an abandoned tab, at the socket drop -- an open tab counts as live. For a refused final submission, datapipe-client stamps the session abandoned IMMEDIATELY (packages/client/src/session.ts, `close({submitted:false})`), so the clock starts at the refusal; whether @jspsych/extension-pipe does the same is not verified, so close the tab promptly afterwards either way. The 24-hour `expiresAt` is the backstop behind both.
timingFacts.observedPageRates: jsPsych page with auto=1: 1.1-1.7 s per trial. Vanilla page with auto=1: 400 ms per trial. A /api/data call that writes to Drive: 2-4.5 s.

knownIssues.summary: On Google Drive, one `.psychds-ignore` file accumulates per successful upload rather than one per experiment. metadata-derived-upload.ts dedupes on the provider's NAME_CONFLICT, and Drive permits duplicate names, so the dedupe never fires.
knownIssues.consequence: Never assert on the TOTAL number of files in the folder. Count the files matching this run's filename stem instead.
knownIssues.observed: 5 copies after 5 uploads, 2026-09-19. A pre-existing DataPipe bug, not a testbed one.

knownIssues.summary: A submission refused with 400 METADATA_ERROR keeps its pending Cloud Storage copy on purpose (api-data.ts: "scheduled-pending-recovery salvages it later instead of losing it outright"). METADATA_ERROR means metadata generation failed, not that the participant's data was refused, and the policy is never to destroy raw data over it.
knownIssues.consequence: Within the next pending-recovery slot (:00/:15/:30/:45, for entries older than ~15 minutes) a queue entry appears for that filename with failureReason "Recovered from interrupted upload (server restart or memory limit)". EXPECT it. Do not flag it. The wording is misleading for this case -- no server restarted.
knownIssues.observed: 3 such entries at 17:15 UTC, 2026-09-19, one per METADATA_ERROR refusal.

knownIssues.summary: metadata-block.ts returns `{...MESSAGES.METADATA_ERROR, message: errorMessage}` -- it overrides the message with the specific failure text, so the wire message for METADATA_ERROR is not the string in api-messages.ts.
knownIssues.consequence: Assert on the `error` code. Never on `message`, for any endpoint.

knownIssues.summary: Loading the jsPsych page starts a session before any trial runs, so a page opened and navigated away from leaves a live-session row behind until the sweep clears it.
knownIssues.consequence: Never assert on the NUMBER of sessions in progress. Match rows by this run's `run` id.

scenarios.title: Data that fails validation
scenarios.description: The plain JavaScript page leaves `trial_type` off every row, so the submission fails the validation rules a new experiment ships with. DataPipe refuses it with `INVALID_DATA` and stores nothing — and, unlike a metadata failure, keeps no copy to recover later.
driverActions: Nothing on the dashboard. This scenario exercises the DEFAULT validation settings, so do not change them.
Open the URL, click the body, then send `f` in a separate call.
`stream=0` on purpose: api-data.ts deliberately leaves staged trials alone on INVALID_DATA, so a streamed run here would leave a recoverable session behind and turn this into a deferred scenario.

notes: a note reading "failvalidation: `trial_type` is omitted from every row on purpose"

expectDashboard: A new error-panel entry with the code INVALID_DATA.
No queue entry, now or later.

expectStorage.completeness: nothing is written, and nothing appears later either: the useValidation block in api-data.ts runs BEFORE persistPending, so no pending copy exists for the recovery sweep to find. That is the contrast with a METADATA_ERROR refusal, which does leave one -- see knownIssues.

timing.checkStorageAfter: n/a -- but re-check at the next :00/:15/:30/:45 slot that NOTHING was queued

scenarios.observed: not run; code-derived. api-data.ts (the useValidation block and its position relative to persistPending), validate-csv.ts and validate-json.ts: both validators check `requiredFields` against the CSV header row / the union of JSON object keys, and with allowCSV and allowJSON both on by default a CSV missing the column fails each in turn.

scenarios.title: Abandoned tab
scenarios.description: Close the tab half-way. Within seconds the dashboard row reads `Connection lost — may resume`; after 10 minutes, `Stopped — being recovered`; the sweep then queues the staged trials, and the `.partial.json` reaches storage about an hour later, not within 15 minutes.
driverActions: Open the URL and let it run to about trial 50 of 60 (roughly 60-80 s).
Read the result and KEEP the first filename FIRST -- it is unrecoverable once the tab is gone, and it is the only way to recognise the partial later.
Close the tab. Note the wall-clock time: the recovery clock starts at the socket drop. An open tab counts as live.

notes: The page never reaches a terminal status: the tab is gone. The last status read before closing must be "running".
sessionId is null on this page -- extension-pipe does not surface it.

expectDashboard: Within seconds of the tab closing: the row for this run reads "Connection lost — may resume".
About 10-12 minutes later: "Stopped — being recovered".
Then the row disappears and a queue entry appears with failureReason "Recovered from an abandoned session (N trials)", status pending, retryCount 0, lastAttemptAt null, nextRetryAt one hour out.

expectStorage.countBy: files matching `<this run's filename stem>-<8 hex>.partial.json`
expectStorage.naming: <submitted filename without its extension>-<8 hex characters>.partial.json. The hash suffix is ALWAYS there -- partialFilenameFor derives it from the session id, not from a name collision.
expectStorage.completeness: partial: only the trials staged before the tab closed
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root, or data/raw/ with metadata on

timing.checkDashboardAfter: immediately, at ~11 min, and at ~14 min
timing.checkStorageAfter: 65-75 minutes after the tab was closed

scenarios.deferredNote: Re-open the folder 75 minutes after the tab was closed and look for one *.partial.json matching this run's filename stem. Until then `GET /api/queuestatus?experimentID=<id>` is better evidence than the dashboard panel: it shows retryCount and lastAttemptAt. A queue entry that has never been attempted is the expected state, not a failure.
scenarios.observed: 2026-09-19 with trials=60, closed at ~50: queued 12 min after the tab closed as `data/raw/testbed-...-6b33aa40.partial.json`, nextRetryAt exactly +60 min, live row transitions as described. PASS up to the queue; the Drive write itself was not waited for.

scenarios.title: Failed final submission
scenarios.description: The page claims the filename first, so DataPipe refuses the real submission as a duplicate. The log shows the save failed, and the staged trials come back later as a `.partial.json` under a hash-suffixed name.
driverActions: Open the URL. If the pre-claim is refused the page now stops with status "failed" and a note instead of running -- that is a FAIL of the scenario, and the note says which code came back.

After the final save is refused, CLOSE THE TAB promptly. datapipe-client stamps the session abandoned at the refusal, but whether extension-pipe does the same is unverified; closing removes the doubt.
Note the wall-clock time of the refusal.
expectDashboard: A new error-panel entry with the code FILE_EXISTS.
Within about 15 minutes of the refusal: a queue entry for `<stem>-<8 hex>.partial.json`.

expectStorage.countBy: files matching this run's filename stem: the pre-claim file, and later the -<8 hex>.partial.json
expectStorage.naming: the pre-claim file under the run's own filename, plus <stem>-<8 hex>.partial.json holding the staged trials
expectStorage.completeness: the pre-claim file holds one placeholder row, not data; the partial holds the real trials
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root, or data/raw/ with metadata on
expectStorage.note: api-data.ts deliberately does NOT discard staging on a duplicate-filename refusal -- that is what makes the partial recoverable. It DOES discard if the experiment is switched off before the sweep gets there; see `ordering`.

timing.checkDashboardAfter: immediately, and again ~15 min after the refusal
timing.checkStorageAfter: the pre-claim file immediately; the partial 65-75 minutes after the refusal

scenarios.deferredNote: Re-check the folder ~75 minutes after the refusal for the .partial.json. The pre-claim file is there straight away and is not the thing under test. Do NOT switch data collection off before this session's partial is visible in /api/queuestatus.
scenarios.observed: 2026-09-19: the testbed's own breaksave was BROKEN -- the pre-claim body was a plain sentence, refused with METADATA_ERROR on a Psych-DS experiment, so the filename was never claimed and the run silently succeeded. Reproduced by hand with a valid one-row CSV pre-claim: 201, then final save 400 FILE_EXISTS, so the refusal half PASSES. The recovery half was invalidated by switching the experiment off too early; see `ordering`. The pre-claim body is fixed in this change and the page now stops loudly if the claim fails.

scenarios.title: Brief dropout
scenarios.description: Go offline for about 30 seconds mid-run, then back online, and finish. The dashboard row flips to `Connection lost — may resume` and back to `In progress`; you get one complete file and no partial.
driverActions: Open the URL and let it run for ~10 seconds.
Put the browser offline for 30 seconds: DevTools network throttling, the OS network toggle, or Playwright's context.setOffline(true).
Go back online and let the run finish.

notes: an `extension-pipe:` note about a failed flush during the offline window is expected, not a failure

expectDashboard: During the offline window: the row for this run reads "Connection lost — may resume".
After reconnecting: back to "In progress" (the reconnect slot heals the disconnect stamp).
After finishing: no row for this run, and no queue entry.

expectStorage.countBy: files matching this run's filename stem -- and confirm there is NO .partial.json for it
expectStorage.naming: the name in the result's filenames
expectStorage.completeness: complete, including the trials recorded while offline
expectStorage.location: experiment folder root, or data/raw/ with metadata on

timing.checkDashboardAfter: during the offline window and again after reconnecting
timing.checkStorageAfter: ~30 s after the page reports finished
timing.note: The offline window must be under 10 minutes or the sweep will treat the session as abandoned.

scenarios.automationNote: The Chrome extension cannot throttle or disable the network, so an agent driving that extension cannot run this. No URL parameter was added to fake it: what is under test is the Realtime Database's own disconnect-and-heal path, and a page-level simulation would exercise neither the onDisconnect stamp nor the reconnect slot that clears it -- it would prove nothing while looking like it had. A Playwright job CAN run it with context.setOffline(true), which makes it the one non-`full` scenario worth putting in a headless job.
scenarios.observed: not run on 2026-09-19: the browser tooling had no way to go offline.

scenarios.title: Closed experiment
scenarios.description: Switch data collection off and run the jsPsych test: no session is started and the final submission is refused with `DATA_COLLECTION_NOT_ACTIVE`.
driverActions: STOP. Confirm first that every recovery-dependent scenario's partial is already QUEUED -- `GET /api/queuestatus?experimentID=<id>` must list an entry for `abandoned-tab` and for `failed-final-submission`. Switching collection off before that DESTROYS them.
Switch "Accept new data" OFF and wait for the "Saved" badge.
Open the URL and let it run.
Switch "Accept new data" back ON afterwards if anything else follows.

notes: a `datapipe:` note that the session was not started; the page cannot see /api/session's status code itself

expectDashboard: No row for this run in "Sessions in progress" at any point.
New error-panel entries with the code DATA_COLLECTION_NOT_ACTIVE (logged twice: once by /api/session, once by /api/data).
scenarios.mutatesExperimentState: turns "Accept new data" OFF -- and while it is off the staging sweep DISCARDS any still-staged session
scenarios.runAfterCondition: each of those scenarios' partials is visible as a queue entry in GET /api/queuestatus?experimentID=<id>
scenarios.observed: 2026-09-19: `datapipe: session not started (HTTP 400)` then final save 400 DATA_COLLECTION_NOT_ACTIVE. PASS -- but running it early is what destroyed the failed-final-submission recovery in that run.
